To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
capillary electromigration techniques can be used to detect PCR‐products directly from clinical samples without any purification or complicated sample preparation steps.

the use of capillary array electrophoresis (CAE) with UV detection can potentially provide significant advantages over current methods for PCR‐based DNA testing with regard to time‐to‐result, labor, and cost.

capillary electrospray ionization mass spectrometry (CE‐ESI‐MS) is a powerful tool for the analysis of complex mixtures of peptides, such as tryptic peptides derived from proteins, or for the analysis of mixtures of synthetic peptides.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and application of capillary electrophoretic methods for high‐throughput genetic analysis of clinical samples.
the development of new methods for high‐throughput analysis of DNA in the field of genetic testing and molecular diagnosis.
the development and application of a novel capillary electrophoretic method for routine genetic analysis of large number of samples.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the use of capillary electrophoretic techniques with UV detection in combination with PCR‐based DNA detection provides a fast, reliable, and inexpensive alternative to current methods for the routine analysis of clinical samples.
this method is very simple, fast, and cost‐effective for the routine genetic analysis of large samples.
capillary electromigration methods are not only useful for the separation and analysis of small amounts of analytes, but also for the analysis of large sample numbers in routine analysis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of capillary electrophoretic techniques with UV detection for the analysis of DNA samples is a promising alternative to current techniques.
the capillary electrophoretic analysis of DNA amplified by PCR from clinical samples is possible with a simple sample preparation and without purification steps.
the combination of PCR with capillary electrophoretic separation and absorption detection is a promising approach for routine clinical DNA analysis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the capillary electrophoretic analysis of PCR products from unprocessed clinical samples can be accomplished with a high level of accuracy and precision.
the capillary electrophoretic separation of DNA fragments can be used for high‐throughput genetic analysis of clinical samples without any additional sample preparation steps.
capillary electromigration can be used for routine genetic analysis of large samples with high‐throughput and high‐resolution.
